subject: Hosted->Dedicated: Safety validation, SLA shadow runs & cutover phases
messages:
From: Sam Ellis <sam.ellis@novadyne.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Upcoming migration to dedicated capacity — initial numbers and timeline

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering team kicked off a sizing doc and attached a rough concurrency / TPS estimate (novadyne_concurrency_estimates.csv). We want to understand what a pragmatic safety-validation path looks like before we commit to the reserved capacity contract. Key asks: 

- A clear sizing attestation step so we can lock commit numbers
- A shadow run window where we can validate P95 latency and error budget without impacting prod
- A short cutover plan with fallbacks in case the swap causes regressions

High-level constraints: procurement needs a signed SOW by Dec 15 to make Q1 budget. Can Redwood provide recommended headroom/instance types and a tight timeline for validation so we can move quickly?

CCing procurement for visibility.

—Sam
Senior Infra Lead, Novadyne

Attachments: novadyne_concurrency_estimates.csv (CSV, 8KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Sam Ellis <sam.ellis@novadyne.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Upcoming migration to dedicated capacity — initial numbers and timeline

Sam — thanks, this is great context. Attaching a draft capacity matrix and a short preflight checklist (redwood_capacity_matrix_v2.xlsx). Proposed validation path (we can iterate):

Phase 0 — Preflight & Sizing Attestation (1 week)
- Redwood produces a headroom-backed sizing recommendation (GPU class + instance count).
- Customer provides representative traffic slice (you already did — thanks).
- Deliverable: Sizing attestation doc and committed capacity figure.

Phase 1 — Shadow SLA Runs (2–3 days)
- We run a no-impact shadow (traffic fork) to measure P50/P95/P99 and error rates.
- Engineer on call both sides.
- Accept criteria: P95 <= agreed SLO + <5% error delta.

Phase 2 — Canary swap (1 day)
- 5–10% traffic or route-specific paths to dedicated. Monitor for 24–48 hours.

Phase 3 — Weekend cutover (window + rollback window)
- Full swap with automated routing fallback to hosted. 4-hour rollback window recommended.

We recommend A100 80GB for the initial profile (unless you need H100 for lower latency on long contexts). Plan for ~30% headroom on estimated peak for first 30 days; we can rightsize post-cutover once we have real telemetry.

Next steps I propose: 1) Redwood sends SOW + runbook draft, 2) we schedule a 60-minute validation planning call tomorrow to lock exact calendar dates, 3) procurement confirms PO timeline.

I can own runbook + scheduling. Monica/E2E: can you confirm availability for the shadow window and canary monitoring?

—Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_capacity_matrix_v2.xlsx (XLSX, 24KB)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Upcoming migration to dedicated capacity — initial numbers and timeline

Sam — quick technical notes from ops: 

- Instance recommendations: start with A100 80GB for throughput-focused inference. If Novadyne needs lower end-to-end latency at 4k+ tokens we can discuss an H100 lane for specific routes.
- Batching: recommend dynamic batching with max_batch_size=64 and target token_latency cap at 50ms for mid-sized prompts.
- Caching: enable prefix KV caching for repeat context sequences; we see 20–35% token savings for similar workloads.
- Autoscaling buffer: assume 30% buffer for traffic spikes for first 2 weeks, then evaluate real usage and reconfigure.

I'll attach a lightweight sizing CSV (derived from your estimates) that maps concurrency to GPU counts and expected P95. We'll use that in the shadow-run acceptance criteria.

If any of these look off to you, tell us now; we can adjust before the attestation.

—Monica
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sizing_lookup_novadyne.csv (CSV, 12KB)

From: Sam Ellis <sam.ellis@novadyne.com>

Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Upcoming migration to dedicated capacity — initial numbers and timeline

Karthik / Monica — this looks reasonable and aligns with what our SREs expect. A couple of clarifications: 

1) Downtime risk: We can't accept more than a 30-minute user-facing outage during the cutover. You mentioned a 4-hour rollback window — can you confirm what actions trigger a rollback, and whether we can automate failover back to hosted immediately?

2) Procurement: We are targeting Dec 15 for signed SOW but we need a short summary (1 page) that our legal/procurement team can review quickly. Can you provide a short SOW summary and a simplified SLA delta document?

3) Canary: we'll prefer a route-level canary first (conversation search path) rather than a percentage-based split — that's easier for our product team to isolate.

If you can send the 1-pager today and propose a concrete shadow week (we're available Dec 7–11), we can lock dates.

Thanks — Sam

Subject: Re: Upcoming migration to dedicated capacity — SOW summary and automated rollback details

Sam — thanks. Attached is a 1-page SOW summary and a short SLA-delta that highlights fallback behavior (sow-dedicated-attachment.pdf). Quick answers: 

- Rollback triggers: sustained P95 > agreed SLO by >20% for 30m OR error-rate increase >3x baseline for 15m. Those thresholds are configurable but are what we typically use for enterprise swaps.
- Failover: we have automated routing policies that will instant-fail traffic back to hosted variants within ~60–120s once triggered; the autopilot includes circuit-breaker cooldowns and an alert flow to both teams.
- Canary routing: supported route-level canaries; we will validate route isolation during the shadow run.

Proposed sample calendar:
- Dec 7: sizing attestation sign-off (deliverable by Redwood EOD Dec 4)
- Dec 8–9: shadow SLA runs (forked traffic, no impact)
- Dec 10: route-level canary (24h watch)
- Dec 11 (Sunday night): final cutover window candidate with 4h rollback window

If Dec 7–11 works, we will finalize and send a signature-ready SOW by EOD today so procurement can start review.

Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4782 — will attach runbook and acceptance matrix there.

—Karthik

Attachments: sow-dedicated-attachment.pdf (PDF, 14KB)
